title: Who Is Noticing?
description: Fifteen minutes looking for whoever is behind the thoughts. An inquiry into non-self.

segments.say: Sit with your back upright but not stiff, and close your eyes.
Let the body settle. Feel the weight, the contact with the ground.
Rest your attention on the breath for a few moments.
In this practice we will ask a question, and not answer it by thinking. Answer it by looking.
Usually it seems there is someone in here. Someone who thinks, who decides, who feels.
The Buddha invited people to look for that someone. Not to deny that you exist, but to see what it is really like.
Start with thoughts.
Wait for the next thought, like a cat waiting at a mouse hole.
Did you choose that thought? Or did it simply appear?
Watch a few more. Where do they come from?
Notice that thoughts happen by themselves. Like sounds, like the breath.
Now notice sounds. They are being heard.
Is there someone hearing? Or is there just hearing?
Now turn your attention around, toward whoever is paying attention.
Look. Where is the one who is noticing? Behind the eyes? In the chest?
Do not accept a ready-made answer. Just look.
If you find something, a sensation, an image, notice: that too is being seen.
So it is not the one who sees. It is one more thing that appears.
Maybe you will not find anyone. Just experience happening, open, without a centre.
This is not a cold emptiness. It is like a window with no one behind it, just light coming in.
Rest there, without needing to understand.
If the sense of me comes back, and it will, that is fine. It is also something that appears.
Now come back to the breath. To the body sitting here.
Take a little of this lightness with you. Less of someone to defend.
When you are ready, open your eyes.
